theorems.name: affine residue-fiber target certificate
assumptions: positive diagonal integer residue layout D
integer affine x->Ax+b
theorems.law: D^-1 A D integral and Ar+b=s mod D iff every point of DZ^6+r maps into DZ^6+s
theorems.boundary: no occupancy or undeclared hidden state

theorems.name: residue/time-port BRC composition
assumptions: HBRC-RP-001
matching residue and time ports
positive exact BRC weights
theorems.law: [r->s;w,A,b] then [s->u;v,B,c]=[r->u;wv,BA,Bb+c]
theorems.boundary: not full labeled-path provenance

theorems.name: finite-word degree-two closure on fixed residue fibers
assumptions: finite invariant residue layout
fiber-constant exact weights
integer affine effects
degree<=2 boundary observer
theorems.law: M'_s=sum_{r,e:r->s} c_e w_e H_e M_r H_e^T, closed under every finite allowed word
theorems.boundary: no arbitrary nonlinear or occupancy observer

theorems.name: even-scale misaligned seam transport
assumptions: F=S_(1,0), G=S_(ell,1), ell even >=2
cycle F,G,F,G
theorems.law: mod 2ell displacement is +2ell on {0,ell+1}, -2ell on {1,ell}, and 0 otherwise; uniform mean absolute displacement is 4
theorems.boundary: diagnostic interaction program, not universal physical heartbeat law

theorems.name: observer-safe residue quotient
assumptions: HBRC-RP-003
same exact effect or moment operator from every merged source into every retained target for every declared future packet
theorems.law: aggregated retained-class moments descend exactly through the quotient for every finite declared operator word
theorems.boundary: certificate scoped to operator family, boundary observer and mode

theorems.name: macro/micro quotient separation
assumptions: mod-4 misaligned cycle C
separable six-axis macrocycle
theorems.law: 1D macro C merges 4 fibers into {0,3}/{1,2}; six-axis macrocycle merges 4096 fibers into 64 effect classes; adding within-cycle F,G invalidates the 1D two-class quotient
theorems.boundary: macro-boundary equivalence is not within-cycle equivalence

theorems.name: fixed residues/current-contact bit do not determine future contact
assumptions: two tagged positions in unbounded Z^6
exact contact observer
signed unit relative moves
theorems.law: no fixed periodic residue labels determine equality; current contact/noncontact alone does not determine next contact
theorems.boundary: not a multi-body collision theorem

theorems.name: coarsest finite-horizon contact quotient
assumptions: relative d in Z^6
all 12 signed unit moves
observe contact after every suffix of length <=h
theorems.law: q_h(d)=d for ||d||_1<=h and FAR otherwise is coarsest; class count=2+sum_{s=1}^{min(6,h)}2^s*C(6,s)*C(h,s); no fixed finite quotient works for all unbounded h
theorems.boundary: FAR is not zero and cannot recover exact far displacement

theorems.name: six-channel dihedral orbit classifier
assumptions: binary six-channel mask in one chosen heartbeat frame
D6 cyclic/reversal relabeling
observer O=(occupied count, adjacent occupied-pair count, opposite occupied-pair count)
theorems.law: The 64 masks form exactly 13 D6 orbits; O is constant on each orbit and has 13 distinct values, hence exactly identifies the orbit quotient.
theorems.boundary: six positive-axis/channel diagnostic mask, not full twelve-direction occupancy

theorems.name: symmetry-safe environment BRC quotient
assumptions: HBRC-ENV-001
future control packets preserve the D6 orbit partition and have identical exact EffectHistogram rows on merged states
theorems.law: The 13 orbit classes are an exact finite control-port BRC quotient for every finite declared symmetry-safe packet word.
theorems.boundary: caller must certify every future packet; observer symmetry alone is insufficient for phase-addressed effects

theorems.name: phase-addressed environment symmetry breaking
assumptions: HBRC-ENV-001
actions R,J plus S0 forcing heartbeat slot0 occupied
theorems.law: T6 predictive block profile is (13,32,52,63,64,64) through horizon5 and stabilizes at all64 masks at depth4; an effect depending on slot0 rejects the 13-class BRC certificate and exact refinement returns64.
theorems.boundary: finite declared mask model; not a universal physical occupancy law

theorems.name: orbit plus orientation-residual decomposition
assumptions: finite D6 action on the 64 six-channel masks
theorems.law: Each raw mask is exactly (orbit, coset modulo its stabilizer); orbit sizes are 1,2,3,6,12. Orientation residual may be omitted only when the declared observer/future descends to the orbit quotient.
theorems.boundary: erased orientation cannot later be recreated; Shannon accounting is not a storage implementation

theorems.name: typed repair-coordinate refinement ladder
assumptions: raw finite control state is residue r mod4 times a 64-mask environment
initial observer partition is 2-class macro residue times 13-class D6 environment quotient
SAFE/MICRO/PHASE packets exactly as documented
theorems.law: Exact effect-valued refinement class counts are 26 for SAFE, 52 after MICRO, 128 after PHASE, and 256 when both MICRO and PHASE are allowed.
theorems.boundary: finite declared packet family; not universal Heartbeat World state complexity

theorems.name: joint-port necessity under coupled effects
assumptions: positive joint distribution on macro residue sign and environment gate
spatial effect couples both variables
theorems.law: Separate residue and environment marginals do not determine the output: two distributions with identical marginals can have mean displacement -2 e1 versus +2 e1. A joint law or exact factorization/independence certificate is required.
theorems.boundary: does not deny marginal sufficiency under separately proved factorization for a specified observer

theorems.name: shared global phase elimination
assumptions: legal phase p is deterministic phi(t) from globally available Heartbeat World time
observer and all declared future operations use p only through t
theorems.law: Projection (x,t,p)->(x,t) is lossless on legal states and all declared future operations descend because p=phi(t) is reconstructed externally.
theorems.boundary: does not apply to local desynchronization or hidden local oscillators

theorems.name: aligned-mask gauge quotient
assumptions: raw state is six-channel local mask m and local offset delta mod6
aligned mask a=R^delta m
future actions descend to aligned physical mask
theorems.law: The 384 raw (m,delta) states form exactly64 free gauge orbits under (m,delta)->(Rm,delta-1); aligned mask is the exact quotient. Orientation-blind D6 futures further admit the13-class shape quotient.
theorems.boundary: six-channel diagnostic; local phase cannot be reconstructed after erasure if later accessed

theorems.name: local-phase access obstruction
assumptions: HBRC-CLOCK-002
future contains a local-frame operation or spatial effect depending on delta
theorems.law: The aligned 64-class quotient is unsafe. In the declared finite model the shape-observer predictive profile becomes (13,113,353,383,384,384), and an effect-valued local-axis packet refines all384 states.
theorems.boundary: finite declared phase model, not a universal physical synchronization law

theorems.name: full typed repair-coordinate ladder
assumptions: finite raw control state r mod4 times six-channel local mask times local offset delta mod6
initial observer is 2-class macro residue times 13-class globally aligned D6 shape
SAFE/ROT/REF/MICRO/ABS/LOCAL packets as documented
theorems.law: Exact effect-valued class counts are 26 under symmetry-safe future, 52 with MICRO, 128 with globally phase-addressed ABS, 256 with MICRO+ABS, 768 with local-phase access, and1536 with MICRO+LOCAL.
theorems.boundary: finite declared product model; class counts are future-language dependent

theorems.name: external-clock state nonmultiplication
assumptions: global heartbeat phase is supplied by the time port
aligned physical mask is retained
macro residue class retained
theorems.law: The product state (macro residue class, aligned mask) has128 classes and is safe for globally framed effects even though the raw local representation has1536 states; a local-axis effect indexed by delta rejects this quotient and exact refinement gives768.
theorems.boundary: does not apply if local offset evolves invisibly or is directly used by future operations

theorems.name: phase-free C6 occupancy observer lattice
assumptions: binary occupancy mask on the six positive native-axis channels
pure cyclic heartbeat relabeling C6 with no material occupancy mutation
compare three explicitly typed observers: total count, C6 orbit shape, and phase-anchored active bit
theorems.law: Under pure rotation: total-count observation has exactly 7 classes for every horizon; phase-free C6 orbit observation has 14 classes (13 after excluding the all-empty background); phase-anchored active-bit futures have 2^min(h+1,6) classes and reach all64 masks at h=5.
theorems.boundary: The three quotients answer different observers. The 14-class C6 shape quotient is not the existing 13-class D6 quotient, and neither is safe when a later operation accesses erased orientation.

theorems.name: use-once occupancy-count future growth
assumptions: same six positive-axis binary mask
each tick marks the currently scanned channel occupied and then advances the cyclic heartbeat
observer records current and future total occupied count through horizon h
theorems.law: For 0<=h<=5 the coarsest future-observation class count is 2^h*(7-h); for h>=5 it is64. Current count plus h successive count increments recovers the first h scanned bits, while the remaining 6-h bits contribute only their total; at h=5 the last bit is fixed by the total.
theorems.boundary: Specific to the declared use-once update and count observer; no general finite environment-memory claim.

theorems.name: strong control-mass lumping preserves all-depth recurrent mass
assumptions: finite nonnegative rational control mass matrix W
partition pi with identical total mass from any two source states in one block into every target block
P is the raw-state to block membership matrix
theorems.law: There is a quotient Q with W P=P Q, hence W^k P=P Q^k for every k. Whenever the all-depth positive mass is finite, W*P=P Q*. Because 1=P1, full and quotient total-mass stability are equivalent under the existing finite recurrent-mass criterion.
theorems.boundary: Mass-only observer. Does not preserve affine effects, target identities inside a block, signed cancellation, path provenance or hidden control.

theorems.name: mass equivalence is strictly weaker than effect equivalence
assumptions: two control states in one candidate block
each has a self branch of weight 1/2
their affine spatial effects differ
theorems.law: The one-block total-mass quotient is exact and has Q=(1/2), while the existing exact effect-valued control certificate rejects the merge. Thus effect equality is sufficient but not necessary for recurrent total-mass equivalence.
theorems.boundary: The merge is safe only for mass observers/futures, not spatial-effect observers.

theorems.name: phase-dependent weights can destroy a symmetry quotient without changing spatial effects
assumptions: two states that an orientation-blind environment observer would merge
identity spatial effect in both states
self weights 1/2 and 3/2
theorems.law: The mass certificate rejects the merge. The first state's all-depth self mass is sum(1/2)^k=2, while the second diverges. Therefore a symmetry quotient valid for geometry alone need not preserve weighted recurrence when branch mass depends on erased phase/environment.
theorems.boundary: Diagnostic positive-mass counterexample, not a physical instability law.

theorems.name: group-equivariant positive kernels lump exactly to environment orbits
assumptions: finite group G acts on control states
nonnegative rational kernel W is G-equivariant: W(gx,gy)=W(x,y)
partition is G-orbits
theorems.law: For x,x' in one orbit and every target orbit B, sum_{y in B}W(x,y)=sum_{y in B}W(x',y); therefore the orbit partition satisfies HBRC-REC-001. A 64-mask D6-equivariant fill/remove/self witness reduces exactly to 13 mass states.
theorems.boundary: Requires kernel equivariance; an invariant current observer alone is insufficient.
